Softbank/ ABB, Apple, Meta, Optimus v3 Google, Meta, and now (reportedly) xAI are building AI World Models - while initial use cases may be in video games - the bigger TAM is in the physical world. Video games are simulations, robots train in simulation. We give the latest on humanoids and more. We provide some updated thoughts on key developments in humanoids & physical AI: • Son: "SoftBank's Next Frontier is Physical AI". SoftBank recently agreed to purchase ABB's Robotics division for $5.4bn after previously planning to spin the business off in light of intensifying competition from Chinese competitors. Softbank founder Masayoshi Son said following the release: "SoftBank’s next frontier is Physical AI. Together with ABB Robotics, we will unite world-class technology and talent under our shared vision to fuse Artificial Super Intelligence and robotics - driving a groundbreaking evolution that will propel humanity forward." SoftBank is already invested in a number of AI/robotics companies including Agile Robots, foundation model developer Skild AI, and others. Could the SoftBank-ABB deal represent the first of many potential tie-ups between major AI investors and legacy robotics/industrials companies? While legacy companies may lack AI talent, they compensate with deep manufacturing and supply chain expertise - something AI-first startups may lack. Meta Making the Android for Androids? In a recent interview with The Verge, Meta's (Covered by Brian Nowak) CTO Andrew Bosworth explained how he sees humanoid robots as Meta's next 'AR-size bet'. Per Bosworth, Meta is currently building a humanoid robot called ‘Meta-Bot’, but long-term wants to be a software/AI provider that can partner with a range of hardware developers globally. META has already formed a robotics team led by Marc Whitten, the former CEO of Cruise, and supported by former Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang who is leading a team to build robot datasets and world models for spatial awareness and dexterity. Meta is not the only company seeking to build the 'Android for Androids'. Google DeepMind recently unveiled their latest Gemini Robotics series of models (Gemini Robotics 1.5) and Genie 3 (Google's latest World Model) was described in its release as "fueling embodied agent research". • World Models - Beyond the Video Game. Elon Musk recently posted on X that "The xAI game studio will release a great AI-generated game before the end of next year." AI gaming startup General Intuition recently raised a $134bn seed round. But consider the opportunities beyond video games that pose a much larger TAMs. Robots learn through physical action or simulated worlds (either pre-training or model-based reasoning for inference). Video games are simulated worlds. Robots represent a major opportunity for world models. It's clear many developers and strategic actors agree. Tesla Optimus v3 Coming 1Q26? On the Tesla 3Q25 earnings call, CEO Elon Musk revealed that Tesla is planning to unveil the fully-redesigned Optimus v3 in 1Q25 (likely Feb or March) which is so human-like "you'll need to poke to believe that it's actually a robot". Musk also gave ambitious production goals of 1 million units for v3, 10 million units for v4, and 50-100 million units for v5. While we think Tesla is likely to be a clear leader in humanoid robots, particularly in the US, we remind investors that development of a transformational technology of this scale is still in the early days. We believe Optimus deployment is likely to remain within Tesla for training/data collection and hardware refinement for at least a few years before being sold at scale externally. Specifically, dextrous hands - the 'holy grail' for the humanoid form factor - is also proving to be one of the most complex electro-mechanical challenges ever faced. A Cook's Hint. Earlier this week, Apple (Covered by Erik Woodring) CEO Tim Cook posted a curious promotional video on X for the company's ongoing "Great Ideas Start on Mac" campaign which included the late Dr. Jane Goodall's voice overlaid on a slide show of various images including children and artists using MacBooks, rapper Tyler the Creator, and an engineer tuning a 1X humanoid robot. The same day, 1X teased a 'major announcement' to happen 10/28. Apple is reportedly making robots (per Bloomberg) as we published last week. A 49 year-old company - making its first product that moves? Neither Apple nor 1X has commented on any potential collaboration, nor do we have any knowledge thereof. Apple reportedly is expected to collaborate with BYD (a Chinese battery and autos company, covered by Tim Hsiao) for the manufacture of its AI-enabled robots. Again, we are not aware of any formal collaboration at this time. China Takes Over Half of 2024 Industrial Robot Installations. The International Federation of Robotics (IFR) recently released their annual World Robotics Report. China represented 54% of 2024 industrial robot installations globally, up from 26% a decade ago, with domestic Chinese suppliers representing over half of sales in their home country for the first time ever. While not specifically humanoids, we view this as another example of how China's national push for advanced manufacturing ('New Productive Forces') has turned the country into a robotics powerhouse.

Figure AI raises $1bn Series C at a $39bn valuation. On Sept 16, Figure announced that it had raised $1bn in committed capital through a Series C round led by Parkway Venture Capital with participation from Brookfield Asset Management, NVIDIA, Macquarie Capital, Intel Capital, Align Ventures, Tamarack Global, LG Technology Ventures, Salesforce, T-Mobile Ventures, and Qualcomm Ventures. Figure stated that the company would use the new capital to scale humanoid robots into homes and commercial operations, build next-gen GPU infrastructure to accelerate training and simulation, and launch advanced data collection efforts (see partnership with Brookfield outlined below).
1X reportedly targeting $1bn fundraising round. According to The Information, household humanoid developer 1X is attempting to raise as much as $1bn, citing sources who spoke to the company's CEO Bernt Bornich. Additionally, the company is aiming for a valuation of at least $10bn. To our knowledge, no one from 1X has commented on the report.

New Robot Models & Hardware Improvements:
Figure unveils 3rd generation Figure 03 humanoid robot. Figure recently unveiled Figure 03, its third-generation humanoid robot engineered from the ground up with a completely redesigned hardware and software architecture. It features enhanced sensory and tactile capabilities, wireless charging, and massmanufacturing readiness, making it suitable for home use, commercial environments, and large-scale deployment. The robot is built to work with Figure’s proprietary AI system ('Helix'), enabling true reasoning and adaptive behavior across tasks, while significantly reducing cost and enabling volume production. Other improvements include faster actuators (2x speeds), higher torque limbs, improved hand dexterity, and extended battery life for sustained operation.
Unitree releases 'H2' full-size humanoid. Unitree recently released the latest generation of its full sized humanoid, dubbed the 'H2'. The robot stands 180cm tall, weighing 70kg with 31 total degrees of freedom (DoF). Uniquely, the robot features an anthropomorphic head/face which can be turned using 2 DoF in the neck. Compute specs include Intel Core i5/i7 for "basic computing power" with an optional Jetson AGX Thor (2,070 TFLOPS) for AI compute.
Agibot released Genie G2 wheel-based humanoids: The G2 is designed for industrial/commercial applications with dexterous hands that have 19 DoF, powered by Agibot’s proprietary large models GO-1 and GE-1 that run on Nvidia Jetson Thor chip. This robot has received order from Joyson Electric and completed first batch of delivery already. Also, Agibot Robotics and Longcheer Technology form a strategic partnership to deploy nearly 1,000 Robots. And under the partnership with PIA Automation, it aims to reach an annual capacity of 3,000 units.
Noetix Robotics to Launch Humanoid Robot Bumi at Rmb9,998 ($1.4k) Limited Offer: Noetix Robotics announced the upcoming release of Bumi, a humanoid robot priced under Rmb10k. Standing 94cm tall and weighing ~12kg, Bumi features a 48V battery (≥3.5Ah) with 1–2 hours endurance. Limited-time pricing of Rmb9,998 will be available during the Double 11–Double 12 sales period on JD.com.
Deep Robotics Releases First Humanoid Robot: Deep Robotics has unveiled its first humanoid robot, DR02. The robot stands 175 cm tall, weighs 75 kg, and features 31 degrees of freedom (excluding end effectors). In the video released by Deep Robotics, DR02 demonstrated full-body waterproof capabilities.

Software/AI Improvements:
xAI to build World Models, first for video games, then for robots? xAI has reportedly begun building World Models, competing with Meta (V-JEPA 2) and Google (Genie 3), initially to create video games, but potentially expanding into robotics over time. The company has reportedly already hired engineers Zeeshan Patel and Ethan He, AI researchers from NVIDIA, who have experience with world models (potentially NVIDIA's Omniverse simulation platform). We note that CEO Elon Musk has also recently posted on X that "The xAI game studio will release a great AI-generated game before the end of next year." xAI is also reportedly hiring video game talent, later confirmed by Musk in a reply on X to an account claiming "xAI is Hiring for Video Games" to which Musk replied "True." We note that both Meta and Google explicitly called out robotics and physical AI as potential use cases in the release of their world models, with NVIDIA also developing the Cosmos world model specifically for robotics. As Tesla prepares to vote on an initial investment in xAI, we ask ourselves if this is just the beginning in the connection between the leading-edge AI-side of the Muskonomy (xAI) and the manufacturing and robotics powerhouse that is Tesla.
Google DeepMind releases latest generation Gemini Robotics models. Google DeepMind recently released the latest version of embodied reasoning models, Gemini Robotics 1.5 and Gemini Robotics ER-1.5. Gemini Robotics 1.5 is claimed to be the company's most capable VLA model yet, translating visual input and natural language instructions into actual motor commands, enabling robots to perform complex tasks in the physical world. Amazon FAR releases ResMimic framework for whole-body humanoid loco manipulation . Amazon's FAR (Frontier AI & Robotics) team recently released ResMimic, a two-stage residual learning framework that builds on a general motion-tracking policy and refines it with task-specific corrections so humanoid robots can perform precise whole-body loco-manipulation. It combines imitation learning with reinforcement fine-tuning, allowing robots to adapt fluidly to new motions and contact dynamics in complex environments. It demonstrated realworld success by enabling a Unitree G1 to carry payloads up to ~5.5 kg (boxes and other objects) with full-body contact and reactive behavior, outperforming prior methods in training efficiency and task success. We note that FAR is a new AI team dedicated to robotics that was launched back in March of this year.
• DOBOT achieved multi-form embodied robot collaboration in real factory scenarios. At CIIF, DOBOT demonstrated its intelligent factory hub coordinating robotic arms, humanoid robots, quadrupeds, and wheeled robots to perform realworld tasks such as material handling, sorting, inspection, delivery, and precision assembly. The company also launched its wheeled humanoid robot, DOBOT ATOM-M.

Sizing the Global Market
We estimate that the global humanoid market could reach nearly $5 trillion in annual revenue by 2050. Assuming a 6 year replacement cycle and the below ASP assumptions, we estimate that the global humanoid market could reach $5 trillion in annual revenue by 2050 ($211 billion by 2035 and $1.2 trillion by 2040). For comparison, in 2024, the 20 largest global auto makers booked an aggregate of ~$2.5 trillion in revenue.
Average Selling Price (ASP) assumptions:
• High Income Countries: We assume that the initial ASP of humanoids was $200k in 2024 (largely research-oriented humanoids), with this declining to $150k each by 2028, and further declines to $50k by ~2040. Post-2040, we assume modest price decreases of ~1% driven by inflation offset by further technological advancements and maturing supply chains. Assume initial ASP's are somewhat inflated given the current lack of domestic supply chains, which get mitigated overtime with onshoring of AI/robotics-enabled manufacturing.
Upper Middle/Lower Middle/Low Income Countries: We assume these humanoids are lower-cost with greater benefits of mass-production, localized supply chains, and production based in cost-efficient countries. Assume meaningful price deflation throughout 2050. We assume an initial ASP of ~$50k (Rmb350k) in 2024, declining to ~$15k (~Rmb100k) by 2050.
